questions.prompt: Which of these is a **continuous** random variable?
options: The time a 3D printer takes to finish a part
The number of misprinted parts in a batch of 50
The number of print jobs queued at 9:00
The number of nozzle clogs in a week
questions.explanation: A time is measured and can take any value in a range, so it is continuous. The other three are counts: discrete, as in Module 4.

questions.prompt: Shaft diameters X are continuous, centered on 25.00 mm. What is P(X = 25.00), the probability that a shaft is **exactly** 25.00 mm?
options: 0, because a single value has no width and so no area under the density
The height of the density at 25.00, because that is the most likely diameter
0.5, because half the shafts are above 25.00 and half below it
1, because 25.00 mm is the mean and every shaft is aimed at it
questions.explanation: For a continuous variable only intervals have probability. The area over one point is 0. The density at 25.00 is a height (probability per mm), not a probability.

questions.prompt: A random variable X has the CDF F(x) = x²/9 for 0 ≤ x ≤ 3. What is P(1 ≤ X ≤ 2)? Give it to three decimals.
An engineer proposes the density f(x) = 0.5 for 0 ≤ x ≤ 3 (and 0 elsewhere). Is it a valid probability density?
options: No. The area under it is 0.5 × 3 = 1.5, and it must be 1
Yes. f(x) is never negative, and 0.5 is below 1
No. A density must be a curve, and this one is flat
Yes. Every value between 0 and 3 is equally likely
questions.explanation: A density needs f(x) ≥ 0 and a total area of 1. This rectangle has area 0.5 × 3 = 1.5. A flat density is fine (the uniform, item 5.2), but its height would have to be 1/3.

questions.prompt: The time X to commission a pump has F(12) = 0.30 and F(18) = 0.85, in hours. What is the probability that commissioning takes between 12 and 18 hours? Give it to two decimals.

The picture shows the reflow times' density with an area shaded. What does the shaded area tell you?
[[figure: st.m5.introduction.eg 1]]
options: The probability that a board takes between 84 and 96 s
The number of boards that take between 84 and 96 s
The probability that a board takes exactly 90 s
The density of the boards between 84 and 96 s
questions.explanation: An area under a density is a probability: here P(84 ≤ X ≤ 96) = 0.6827. It is not a count, and no single time has a probability above 0.
